title: Renoprotective effects of lycopene against acrylamide-induced nephrotoxicity in rats: modulation of oxidative/nitrosative stress, inflammation, apoptosis, mitochondrial dysfunction, and Nrf2/Keap1/HO-1/NQO1 signaling
content:
Abstract
Acrylamide is a food-borne toxicant that induces renal injury through oxidative stress, inflammation, apoptosis, and mitochondrial dysfunction. This study investigated the protective effects of lycopene against acrylamide-induced nephrotoxicity in rats and explored the associated molecular mechanisms. Forty male rats were randomly allocated into four groups (n = 10/group): control, lycopene (10 mg/kg body weight), acrylamide (50 mg/kg body weight), and lycopene + Acrylamide. Treatments were administered orally for 30 consecutive days. Serum renal function and injury biomarkers, urinary renal injury markers, renal oxidative/nitrosative stress indices, antioxidant enzymes, ATP level, inflammatory cytokines, apoptotic markers, histopathological alterations, and renal mRNA expression of CYP2E1, NF-κB, COX-2, KIM-1, Nrf2, Keap1, HO-1, and NQO1 were evaluated. Acrylamide significantly increased serum urea, creatinine, cystatin-C, KIM-1, and NGAL, as well as urinary albumin, albumin/creatinine ratio, urinary KIM-1, and urinary NGAL, while reducing urinary creatinine. Acrylamide also elevated renal ROS, 4-HNE, MDA, NO, 8-OHdG, TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, and Bax, and reduced GSH, SOD, CAT, GPx, ATP, and Bcl-2. Marked renal histopathological lesions accompanied these changes. At the molecular level, acrylamide upregulated CYP2E1, NF-κB, COX-2, KIM-1, and Keap1 expression and downregulated Nrf2, HO-1, and NQO1 expression. Lycopene co-treatment significantly attenuated these biochemical, urinary, histopathological, inflammatory, apoptotic, mitochondrial, and gene expression alterations. Lycopene protects against acrylamide-induced nephrotoxicity by improving renal function, reducing oxidative/nitrosative stress and DNA damage, restoring antioxidant and ATP levels, suppressing inflammation and apoptosis, and modulating CYP2E1/NF-κB/COX-2/KIM-1 and Nrf2/Keap1/HO-1/NQO1-related gene expression.
